summary: 630-line Python tool that lets an AI agent autonomously run ML experiments: agent edits train.py, runs a fixed training job, keeps change if val_bpb improves, reverts otherwise. ~12 experiments/hour, ~100 overnight. Released March 7, 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the accept-only-if-score-improves feedback loop is conceptually related to AgentForge's self-score/distillation pattern, but the model is benchmark-driven rather than issue-driven. No verified gap; HID-186 and HID-188 cover adjacent concerns.

summary: MIT-licensed Go plugin for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex CLI that autonomously discovers, builds, audits, and ships improvements to any codebase. Last active June 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — targets the same CLI agent toolchain AgentForge uses; the autonomous self-improvement loop parallels the skill distillation pipeline, which is already shipped. Backlog was full this run; no verified gap beyond shipped features.

summary: Multi-agent episodic context reconstruction for LLM memory. Hierarchical architecture: subordinate agents hold uncompressed episode windows, master agent orchestrates retrieval. Draws on biological engrams.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly relevant to HID-188 (cross-run episodic memory injection into planner/executor). HID-188 already tracks this theme; no new issue needed.

summary: Stores memory items across four graph types (semantic, temporal, causal, entity), keeping episode windows intact under subordinate agents rather than compressing to summaries. Highest LoCoMo score ~0.7 as of early 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — richer memory graph representation could enhance HID-188, but adds significant infrastructure complexity. HID-188 already covers the core gap.

summary: Splits dialogue history into working, episodic, persona, and graph-based memory components. Adaptive memory system designed for long-running dialogue agents.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — multi-tier memory maps to AgentForge's skill distillation + HID-188 episodic memory work. No new gap verified beyond HID-188.

summary: AutoGen successor from Microsoft, reached 1.0 on April 3 2026 for Python and .NET. AutoGen repo is now in maintenance mode; AG2 is the community fork continuing the original line.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses Claude Code and Codex as CLI subprocesses, not Python SDK agents. MAF is an alternative orchestration layer, not a component AgentForge would adopt.

summary: ~900-line TypeScript tool that reviews coding agent session logs, identifies behavioral friction, and edits the agent's rules. MIT-licensed iterative self-improvement harness for coding agents.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — session-log review and rule editing is conceptually similar to skill distillation, which is already SHIPPED in AgentForge (distillationAgent.ts, agentSkillRepository.ts). No new gap.

summary: RL-trained code LLM that shifts from external-dependent refinement to intrinsic autonomous self-reflection and self-correction at inference time. Accepted ACL 2026 Findings.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — this is a model training technique, not an orchestration pattern. AgentForge uses off-the-shelf CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex) and cannot train underlying models.

summary: Karpathy coined 'agentic engineering' on No Priors podcast (March 2026): humans keep architectural responsibility, agents do execution. Hasn't manually coded since Dec 2025.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — conceptual framing, not an implementable technique. AgentForge already embodies this model (human approves plans, agents implement).

summary: LangGraph released v1.2 (May 2026); CrewAI reached v1.15.1. Both continuing active development. No breakthrough capability changes identified in secondary sources; primarily API polish and performance.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge does not use either framework. Version bumps with no breakthrough patterns don't warrant adoption evaluation.
